title: NY State Senate · District 27
area: Lower Manhattan (East Village, Gramercy, Lower East Side, Chinatown, Financial District, Battery Park City) and northwest Brooklyn (Brooklyn Heights, DUMBO, Williamsburg, Greenpoint).

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Brian Kavanagh (D) did not file for re-election. Assemblymember Grace Lee defeated former Assemblymember Yuh-Line Niou 62.5%-37.3% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary.

Niou separately won the Working Families Party primary, but Ballotpedia lists her as a withdrawn/disqualified candidate for the general election; she does not appear on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot, which is a two-candidate race between Lee and Jason Murillo.

candidates.name: Grace Lee
candidates.currentRole: New York State Assemblymember, District 65 (since 2023); not seeking re-election to the Assembly

summary.text: Grace Lee is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for the open NY Senate District 27 seat. She is the Assemblymember for District 65 (Lower Manhattan), first elected in 2022, and describes a background as a co-founder of a parent-led environmental coalition and of a beauty products company. According to the Assembly, she is the first Korean American woman elected to the New York State Legislature and chairs the Assembly Asian Pacific American Task Force; she is not seeking re-election to her Assembly seat.

background.text: Daughter of immigrants, according to her Assembly biography; has lived in Lower Manhattan for about 15 years per her 2020 Ballotpedia survey, and lives there with her husband and three young daughters.
Earned a B.A. in economics and philosophy from Columbia University (2002) and an M.B.A. in finance and entrepreneurship from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business (2010).
In 2018, according to her 2020 survey, she was the New York events director for Swing Left, a group focused on flipping the U.S. House.

Co-founded Children First, a parent-led coalition focused on mercury brownfield cleanup near the South Street Seaport, and co-founded Nine Naturals, a beauty products company, before running for office.
Ran for Assembly District 65 in 2020 and lost the Democratic primary to incumbent Yuh-Line Niou.

Won the June 2022 Democratic primary for the open Assembly District 65 seat and the November general election over Republican Helen Qiu, taking office in January 2023; re-elected in 2024 with 99.1% of the vote.
Serves on the Assembly's Banks, Children and Families, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Environmental Conservation, and Insurance committees, and chairs the Asian Pacific American Task Force.
According to her Assembly biography, she sponsored the Hate Crimes Modernization Act and led legislation making New York the first state to recognize Lunar New Year as a statewide school holiday.
Defeated former Assemblymember Yuh-Line Niou in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for Senate District 27, 62.5% to 37.3%.

priorities.text: Housing affordability: protect rent-stabilized tenants and expand emergency rental assistance, having secured nearly $400 million through ERAP for NYCHA and Section 8 residents.
Universal childcare and expanded pre-K, building on $2 billion in statewide childcare investments she says she helped secure ($350 million for NYC).
Limit state and local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement (ICE), including barring ICE from schools, hospitals, and places of worship.
Raise taxes on the highest earners and close corporate tax loopholes, including support for a pied-a-terre tax on second homes valued at $5 million or more.
Expand access to healthcare, including co-sponsoring the New York Health Act to create a universal single-payer system and lowering prescription drug costs.

positions.summary: Campaign platform supports Good Cause Eviction protections against unreasonable rent increases and retaliatory evictions, and funding legal services for tenants facing harassment.

Platform calls for ending most state and local cooperation with ICE, banning contracts between local jails and ICE, and keeping ICE out of schools, hospitals, and places of worship; co-sponsors the New York for All Act.
Supports higher income-tax rates on the highest earners, a wealth tax on the richest households, closing corporate tax loopholes, and a surcharge on second homes valued at $5 million or more.
Co-sponsors the New York Health Act to establish a universal single-payer healthcare system and supports a state-funded essential plan for low- and moderate-income New Yorkers.
Platform states she is fighting for statewide universal childcare access, citing past work securing billions in statewide childcare investment.
Platform supports a statewide clean fuel standard for transportation, expanding NYPA's renewable-power role, and requiring corporate emissions transparency.

Platform supports protecting the privacy of abortion providers and patients, backed the 2024 reproductive-freedom ballot measure, and says she helped secure $25 million for the state's Abortion Access Program.
Platform supports Manhattan congestion pricing while seeking an exemption for Lower and Midtown Manhattan residents earning under $60,000.

record.text: Sponsored and helped pass the Hate Crimes Modernization Act, described by her office as the first update to New York's hate crimes statute in more than two decades.
Led the legislative effort making New York the first state to designate Lunar New Year as a statewide school holiday.
Introduced the STOP Act, aimed at increasing institutional accountability following the conduct findings against former Governor Andrew Cuomo.
Says she secured nearly $400 million in Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP) funding for NYCHA and Section 8 households in her first year in office (2023).

Chairs the Assembly's Asian Pacific American Task Force and serves on the Banks, Children and Families, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Environmental Conservation, and Insurance committees in the 2025-2026 session.

summary.text: Jason Murillo is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee for the open NY Senate District 27 seat. A Lower East Side native known as "DJ Loud Mouth" in radio and media, he is listed by Ballotpedia as a politician/attorney. He ran for NYC Council District 2 in 2025 and lost the general election, and was listed as a withdrawn or disqualified candidate in the February 2026 special election for Assembly District 74.

background.text: Born in New York, NY; graduated from Seward Park High School.

Describes himself as a lifelong Lower East Side/East Village resident and, under the name "DJ Loudmouth," a media producer and radio host with about 20 years in television and radio, including programming on WPAT 930 AM, per his 2024 Ballotpedia survey. Ballotpedia lists his profession as politician/attorney.

Describes himself in that survey as a Manhattan Republican Party member, chair of the Manhattan Young Conservatives Club, a community board member, and a 74th Assembly District leader and leader of the Manhattan Conservative Party; the survey gives both current and former district leader titles.
Was the Republican and Conservative candidate for New York City Council District 2 in November 2025, losing to Harvey Epstein (D/WFP), 78.0% to 16.5%.

Was listed as a withdrawn or disqualified Republican/Conservative candidate in the February 3, 2026 special election for NY Assembly District 74, won by Keith Powers (D); he did not appear on that ballot.
Advanced to the general election for Senate District 27 after the June 23, 2026 Republican and Conservative primaries were canceled.

priorities.text: Says he is for smaller, more fiscally responsible government and opposes tax increases he describes as excessive and burdensome on working families and small businesses.
priorities.quote: I'm not a fan of big government and overspending, raising taxes and unnecessary and excessive taxes that hurts hard working New Yorkers & small businesses, families who are already struggling to survive in these hard times.

priorities.text: Says he has long advocated for people with disabilities and for supportive services and funding for public housing, low-income families, veterans and the elderly.
priorities.quote: Protecting & safeguarding Public Housing & NYCHA fighting for resident rights to affordable housing for all especially those of low income & hard working families, the disabled, homeless & veterans.

researchNotes: Jason Murillo has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey for this Senate race and has no prior officeholding record or current campaign website; his priorities here come from the Candidate Connection survey he completed in 2024 for his 2025 NYC Council District 2 campaign, still displayed on his Ballotpedia page (checked https://ballotpedia.org/Jason_Murillo on 2026-09-25); a fact-check removed a tax_wealthy position drawn from generic anti-tax-increase language in that survey, since it did not address taxes on high earners or corporations specifically, so no positions are recorded for him. Per Ballotpedia, Yuh-Line Niou won the June 2026 Working Families Party primary for this seat but is listed as withdrawn/not appearing on the November 3 general-election ballot, superseding the July 2026 snapshot data that showed her as a WFP-line general-election candidate; she is therefore not included as a candidate in this file. Murillo's biography relies on Ballotpedia and his self-reported 2024 survey; no campaign website or news profile was found, and his survey gives inconsistent district-leader titles and does not describe a law degree or bar admission.
